name: Fall Silent
label: Revelation
lede: Reno's angriest band got beaten up for one song in Salt Lake City, got famous in Japan because Max Ward wore their shirt, crashed out of its last tour in New Jersey, and came back with a math teacher on vocals.

eras.title: Crowbar fans in the high desert
eras.text: Brothers Levi Watson and Damon Watson came out of New Blood; Danny Galecki and Brian Wohlgemuth came out of Sister Mary 12". Together in Reno they wanted Crowbar, '90s death metal and '80s punk in the same song, and the first 7" wouldn't even play at the right speed.

years.h: Fall Silent form in Reno, Nevada
years.p: Levi Watson sings, his brother Damon Watson drums, Danny Galecki plays guitar and names the band, and Brian Wohlgemuth plays bass.
Fall Silent's self-released debut 7": 500 pressed, with technical trouble around its 45 rpm format. A split 7" with Wellington follows on Fetus Records, run through Ryan Butler, later of Unruh.

years.h: No Strength to Suffer · Revolutionary Power Tools
years.p: Seventeen songs, recorded at Sierra Sonics and self-released under the RPT name. Revelation later called Fall Silent possibly the angriest band around.
years.xp: The album brought odd timing, more dynamics and more technical guitar parts, with Crowbar and Meshuggah in the mix.

q: It was the most fun we had on any tour we ever did.
years.h: Fall Silent tour the US with [[Gehenna|50aaf1dc-2528-4d34-b4a1-262b9b959751]]
years.p: About twenty shows across the country behind No Strength to Suffer, including a CBGB matinee and Epicenter in San Francisco with [[Spazz|30185d89-e9b1-4083-8a58-4688e10e0ec8]]. Levi Watson calls it the most fun tour they ever did.

years.big: $1,800 in merch money, gone in Salt Lake City
q: I got beat up really bad in Salt Lake City for playing that song.
years.h: Fall Silent's song Looking In gets them attacked in Salt Lake City
years.p: Levi Watson wrote Looking In against Reno's violent hardline straight edge kids; plenty heard it as anti-straight edge. In Salt Lake City, Watson says, he was badly beaten for playing it.
years.xp:
Watson says members of Unconquered and their friends stole $1,800 of Fall Silent's merch money, broke out their car windows and slashed their tires.

He still insists it's an anti-hardline song, not an anti-straight edge one, and Fall Silent still play it.

eras.title: Big in Japan
eras.text: Fall Silent never got big at home, but in Japan they had a following from the first 7" on. Levi Watson credits a single photo of Spazz's Max Ward wearing a Fall Silent shirt.

years.p: Fall Silent's second album, complete with a [[Journey|abd506e1-6f2b-4d6f-b937-92c267f6f88b]] cover. Japan gets its own edition with full lyric translations, and 702 and Slovenly put it on vinyl in 1999.

years.h: Life: Beautiful, But Heartless 7" on Max Ward's label
years.p: Released through [[Spazz|30185d89-e9b1-4083-8a58-4688e10e0ec8]] drummer Max Ward and widely spread in Japan. It's bassist Roger Colestock's last recording with Fall Silent.

years.h: Fall Silent's first overseas tour: Japan
years.p: Levi Watson thinks a photo of Max Ward in a Fall Silent shirt on a Spazz record is about 80% of why Japan loves them. Japanese fans, he says, had better venues, better merch and bought CDs.

eras.title: Revelation, a crash in New Jersey
eras.text: Revelation gathered Fall Silent's out-of-print records and put out a new album with two younger death metal fans in the band. Then the tour ended in a wreck in New Jersey, and the band came apart.

years.p: A remastered CD collecting No Strength to Suffer, Nineteenhundredninetyseven and the Life: Beautiful, But Heartless 7". Levi Watson's son is born the same year.

years.h: Live at the Stork Club, Oakland, 2001
yt: Live at the Stork Club, Oakland, 2001

years.p: Produced by Eric Stenman, with second guitarist Donny Johnson and bassist Justin Spalin. Their love of death metal pushes Fall Silent straighter and heavier, with fewer odd time signatures.

years.h: Levi Watson crashes Fall Silent's vehicle in New Jersey
years.p: The US tour behind Drunken Violence ends early when Levi Watson crashes the band's vehicle in New Jersey. He dates the beginning of the end to that wreck.

Levi Watson lists the reasons: a new son, a marriage ending, the failed 2002 tour, a band drifting apart, and Damon Watson's struggles with substances. At the time he never wanted to do Fall Silent again.

eras.title: Mr. Watson, math teacher
eras.text: Levi Watson went back to school and taught math for twelve years, winning awards for it. Damon Watson moved home from Seattle and started Old Glory with Danny Galecki, and the two of them talked Levi back.

years.h: Fall Silent's unannounced reunion at a Reno bar
years.p: The day after Christmas, with no advance promotion, Levi Watson, Damon Watson and Danny Galecki play as Fall Silent again at a local Reno bar.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history
years.p: Fall Silent's first new music since 2002, mastered by Ryan Butler at Arcane Digital. Levi Watson picks Try Harder as the song that sums up the band: grind, thrash and punk in one.
years.xp: Revelation pressed 330 on gold and 770 on red/black marble. Joe Foley joined on guitar, with a two-guitar line-up planned.

years.h: Fall Silent back in Japan, with a 15-year-old merch guy
years.p: Seventeen years after their first Japan tour, Fall Silent return. Levi Watson brings his son Jude, 15, to sell merch. A Japanese band called Superstructure puts Fall Silent's album art on its merch and hosts an annual No Strength to Suffer festival.

eras.title: You Knew I Was Poison
eras.text: Fall Silent's first album in nearly two decades came out in the middle of the pandemic, with Joe Foley now on bass. Fans still couldn't get the old records on vinyl, and one of them tried to do something about it.

years.p: Eight songs from Levi Watson, Damon Watson, Danny Galecki and Joe Foley. Two Plus Two Is Five takes on reading the Bible literally.
years.xp: Revelation pressed 300 on red, plus a RevHQ-only white/black splatter of 100 that sold out. Watson, by then a middle school math teacher, said his wife's piercing studio had been shut ten weeks by the pandemic.

years.h: A petition asks Revelation for Fall Silent on vinyl
years.p: A fan starts a Change.org petition asking Revelation to press Six Years in the Desert and Drunken Violence on vinyl, CD-only since the early 2000s. It closes with 27 supporters.
